{"post_text":"**Photon is like a turbocharger for Spark, but only when you’re already in the right gear.**

When I migrated 10 TB of healthcare logs to Delta Lake, I turned on Photon with
`SET spark.databricks.optimizer.photon.enabled = true` and saw a 2× speed‑up on
partition‑aware range‑scan queries. The same 500M record ETL that used to run 40 % slower dropped to 15 % of the previous runtime.

But Photon isn’t a silver bullet. It shines on pure SQL and built‑in Spark functions. When we pushed a custom PySpark UDF to normalise patient codes, Photon ignored it and the job hit the same wall as before. Adding `spark.sql("SET spark.databricks.optimizer.photon.maxUDFs = 0")` forced the engine to skip optimization, keeping the runtime stable.

Also, for streaming with Kinesis, Photon’s advantage disappears because it only optimises batch workloads. I kept the default Spark engine there.

Bottom line: enable Photon for large, read‑heavy Delta Lake pipelines with standard functions. Disable it for heavy UDFs or streaming.

**Have you encountered a scenario where Photon actually hurt performance?**
